title: Fabric Mirroring from Source to OneLake
purpose: Trace baseline and incremental database replication into Delta and downstream analytical consumption.
accessibleSummary: A supported source supplies a baseline and ongoing changes. Managed mirroring merges them into Delta in OneLake. SQL, Direct Lake, Spark, and other consumers query the replica.
longDescription: The operational source remains authoritative. Mirroring establishes a baseline, captures ongoing changes, and maintains Delta tables in OneLake without user-authored ETL. Analytical consumers query the replica. Freshness monitoring loops back to replication operations.

nodes.label: Operational source
nodes.summary: A supported database remains the transactional system of record.
nodes.detail: A supported database remains the transactional system of record. Validate connectivity and establish replication.
nodes.whyItMatters: An authorized source ready for mirroring depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Database mirroring supports a defined set of operational and analytical sources.

inputs: Supported database, selected tables, and credentials
outputs: An authorized source ready for mirroring
drill.example: Azure SQL continues serving writes while orders are mirrored.
failureModes: Assuming every source feature is supported

nodes.label: Initial snapshot
nodes.summary: Mirroring establishes a baseline before ongoing changes are meaningful.
nodes.detail: Mirroring establishes a baseline before ongoing changes are meaningful. Read baseline and establish table sync state.
nodes.whyItMatters: Initial replicated table state depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

processing: Read baseline and establish table sync state
drill.example: Customers are copied once before updates are merged.

nodes.label: Managed change replication
nodes.summary: Fabric continuously applies source changes without user-authored ETL.
nodes.detail: Fabric continuously applies source changes without user-authored ETL. Poll with backoff, stage increments, and merge changes.
nodes.whyItMatters: Updated target tables depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Managed mirroring polls or receives changes and merges incremental files into Delta.

inputs: Source change feed or landing data
processing: Poll with backoff, stage increments, and merge changes
drill.example: An order update is captured and merged into its replica.
failureModes: Schema or key incompatibility stalls a table

nodes.label: OneLake Delta replica
nodes.summary: Replicated data is stored as Delta away from transaction processing.
nodes.detail: Replicated data is stored as Delta away from transaction processing. Commit changes as Delta versions.
nodes.whyItMatters: Reusable analytical replica depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Database mirroring materializes replicated data as Delta in OneLake.

drill.example: Sales tables become available without another export.
failureModes: Retention is shorter than recovery expectations

nodes.label: Analytical consumers
nodes.summary: SQL, Direct Lake, Spark, and other workloads read the replica.
nodes.detail: SQL, Direct Lake, Spark, and other workloads read the replica. Query through the appropriate analytical surface.
nodes.whyItMatters: Reports, queries, notebooks, and products depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Mirrored Delta supports Direct Lake, cross-database SQL, Spark, and other consumers.

processing: Query through the appropriate analytical surface
drill.example: Direct Lake reports orders while Spark builds features.
failureModes: Presenting replication lag as transactionally current
